title: Donald Trump's Life Journey: Queens to the White House Twice
hook: Only one man before him had ever lost the White House, left, and then been sworn back in.
thumbnail_picture: Big close shot on the right side: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark overcoat raises his right hand to take an oath, his other hand resting on a thick closed leather Bible with no lettering, face fierce and determined, inside a grand marble rotunda glowing with golden light. The left third of the frame is empty dark blue shadow.
description:
Donald Trump's life story, from his childhood in Queens to his second inauguration in January 2025. This is the full, neutral timeline of how a builder's son turned his name into a brand, and a brand into a political career.

Follow the journey: military school, Fred Trump's real estate empire, the Grand Hyatt and Trump Tower, The Art of the Deal, the Atlantic City debts and bankruptcies, The Apprentice, the 2016 upset, two impeachments, January 6, the New York conviction, the Butler assassination attempt, and the return in 2025 as the second president after Grover Cleveland to serve two non-consecutive terms.

Sources and further reading:
- Gwenda Blair, The Trumps: Three Generations That Built an Empire
- Michael D'Antonio, Never Enough: Donald Trump and the Pursuit of Success
- U.S. Senate records on the impeachment trials of 2020 and 2021 (senate.gov)
- National Archives, Electoral College results for 2016, 2020 and 2024
tags: trump from queens to white house

scenes.narration: Only one man before him had ever lost the White House, left, and then been sworn back in.
scenes.caption: JANUARY 2025
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark overcoat raises his right hand inside a grand marble rotunda, a woman holds a thick closed Bible before him, solemn faces, golden light under a high dome.

scenes.narration: On January 20, 2025, he took the oath inside the Capitol Rotunda, because forecasters predicted dangerously cold weather.
scenes.caption: INSIDE THE CAPITOL
scenes.picture: The white domed Capitol building on a frozen winter morning, frost on empty rows of outdoor chairs, pale icy sunlight, bare trees.

scenes.narration: But nearly a decade earlier, when he launched his campaign, few experts gave him a chance. So how did a builder's son from Queens get here?
scenes.caption: THE QUESTION
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark suit and long red tie stands on a high balcony looking out over the Manhattan skyline at dusk, thoughtful face.

scenes.narration: Maybe it comes down to one big idea: that a name can be worth more than the buildings it's attached to.
scenes.caption: THE BIG IDEA
scenes.picture: A gleaming gold-glass skyscraper towering over Manhattan at sunrise, its glass walls blazing with light, seen from low on the street.

scenes.narration: It begins in Queens, New York, where Donald Trump was born on June 14, 1946.
scenes.caption: QUEENS, 1946
scenes.picture: A quiet 1940s Queens street of red brick houses and parked old cars, a mother in a 1940s dress carrying a baby wrapped in a blanket up the front steps.

scenes.narration: His father, Fred, built apartment blocks across Queens and Brooklyn, so he took his young son along to the building sites.
scenes.caption: FRED TRUMP
scenes.picture: A stern man in a 1950s suit and hat holds rolled blueprints, a small blond boy in short pants, young Donald Trump, beside him, red brick apartment buildings rising behind them with scaffolding.

scenes.narration: By his own account, the boy picked up Fred's habits: watch every cost, buy land, promote what you build. Fred's money and bank guarantees helped early on, too.
scenes.caption: LESSONS FROM FRED
scenes.picture: Close-up of a large weathered hand pointing at a rolled blueprint on a wooden desk, a boy's hand resting beside it, brick buildings visible through a window.

scenes.narration: But by thirteen, the boy was getting into trouble, so his parents sent him to New York Military Academy.
scenes.caption: MILITARY SCHOOL
scenes.picture: Thirteen-year-old Donald Trump, a blond cartoon boy, in a gray cadet uniform and cap stands stiffly at attention on a parade ground before a grand stone academy building, rows of cadets behind.

scenes.narration: He learned discipline there, graduated in 1964, and went on to study at Fordham and then the Wharton School.
scenes.caption: COLLEGE YEARS
scenes.picture: Young Donald Trump in his twenties, a recognisable cartoon caricature (thick swept blond hair, broad face), in a 1960s jacket and tie carries books across a leafy brick university campus in autumn, other students walking in the background.

scenes.narration: In 1968 he came home with a degree and one plan: join Fred's company.
scenes.picture: Young Donald Trump in his twenties, a recognisable cartoon caricature (thick swept blond hair, broad face), in a 1960s suit walks through the door of a brick office building, his stern father waiting inside with his arms crossed.

scenes.narration: But Fred's world was Queens and Brooklyn. Across the river, Manhattan was where the money and the cameras were.
scenes.caption: ACROSS THE RIVER
scenes.picture: Young Donald Trump in his twenties, a recognisable cartoon caricature (thick swept blond hair, broad face), in a 1970s suit stands on a Queens riverbank at dusk, gazing across the water at the glittering Manhattan skyline.

scenes.narration: So in 1971 he became president of the family firm, with Fred still chairman, and he started crossing that river.
scenes.caption: TAKING CHARGE
scenes.picture: Young Donald Trump in his twenties, a recognisable cartoon caricature (thick swept blond hair, broad face), in a 1970s suit sits behind a large desk in an office, a window behind him showing the Manhattan skyline.

scenes.narration: His first big target was the Commodore, a run-down hotel beside Grand Central Terminal, in a city close to bankruptcy.
scenes.caption: THE COMMODORE
scenes.picture: A shabby, grimy old brick hotel beside a great stone train terminal, litter on the sidewalk, dim yellow street lamps, gloomy 1970s mood.

scenes.narration: So he made a deal. Hyatt would partner with him, and the city would give him a huge tax break.
scenes.caption: THE DEAL
scenes.picture: Two men in 1970s suits shake hands across a polished conference table, city officials seated behind them, a model of a hotel on the table.

scenes.narration: It worked. The Grand Hyatt opened in 1980, its mirrored glass front reflecting the old terminal. Manhattan had a new builder.
scenes.caption: GRAND HYATT, 1980
scenes.picture: A tall hotel with a shimmering mirrored glass front reflecting the old stone train terminal beside it, glowing in golden afternoon light.

scenes.narration: Next, he aimed higher, at Fifth Avenue, buying the Bonwit Teller site beside the famous jeweler Tiffany, plus Tiffany's air rights, for a tower.
scenes.caption: FIFTH AVENUE
scenes.picture: An old stone department store on Fifth Avenue in 1980 being demolished, a wrecking crane and dust, elegant shoppers watching from the sidewalk, young Donald Trump in his twenties, a recognisable cartoon caricature (thick swept blond hair, broad face), in a suit and hard hat studying it.

scenes.narration: Trump Tower opened in 1983, with pink marble inside, a waterfall, and his own name on the front.
scenes.caption: TRUMP TOWER, 1983
scenes.picture: Inside a lavish atrium with pink marble walls and a tall waterfall cascading down, elegantly dressed visitors gazing up at shiny brass balconies.

scenes.narration: That was the turn. He wasn't only building towers anymore. He was building a brand, and putting his name on it.
scenes.caption: THE BRAND
scenes.picture: A tall black glass skyscraper on Fifth Avenue at night, its entrance glowing with warm golden light, a limousine waiting at the curb.

scenes.narration: Reporters loved him. Magazines put him on their covers, and the builder from Queens became a New York celebrity.
scenes.caption: CELEBRITY
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a sharp 1980s suit and red tie poses in front of a few photographers with big flashing cameras on a Manhattan sidewalk.

scenes.narration: Then in 1987 came a book, The Art of the Deal, written with journalist Tony Schwartz. It became a bestseller, and his name reached well beyond New York.
scenes.caption: THE BOOK, 1987
scenes.picture: A tall stack of identical blue hardcover books with blank covers on a bookstore table, shoppers in 1980s clothes reaching for them.

scenes.narration: Plenty of readers who had never seen his buildings now knew his name.
scenes.caption: A HOUSEHOLD NAME
scenes.picture: An ordinary family in 1980s clothes sit on a living room couch, a father holding a hardcover book and smiling, a TV glowing nearby.

scenes.narration: Riding that fame, he bought bigger, mostly with borrowed money: Atlantic City casinos, an airline, a yacht, and the Plaza Hotel.
scenes.caption: BUYING BIG
scenes.picture: A huge white luxury yacht cruising at sunset beside a glittering seaside casino tower with golden lights, calm sea, seagulls.

scenes.narration: In 1990 he opened the Taj Mahal casino in Atlantic City, at a cost of about a billion dollars.
scenes.caption: THE TAJ MAHAL
scenes.picture: A giant casino resort with golden onion domes and minarets glowing against a night sky by the Atlantic City boardwalk, bright lights.

scenes.narration: But it all ran on borrowed money. When the economy slowed, the casinos couldn't earn enough to pay the interest.
scenes.caption: BORROWED MONEY
scenes.picture: A nearly empty casino floor with rows of idle slot machines and a few bored gamblers, Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a suit standing among them.

scenes.narration: The Taj Mahal went bankrupt in 1991, and over the years more of his casinos and hotels followed.
scenes.caption: BANKRUPTCY
scenes.picture: Stern bankers in gray suits sit around a long boardroom table covered in thick piles of paper, Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a red tie facing them.

scenes.narration: So he gave up the airline and the yacht, handed over stakes in his properties, and negotiated with the banks to stay afloat.
scenes.caption: STAYING AFLOAT
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a rumpled suit hands a ring of keys to a banker across a desk, a model yacht and toy airplane sitting on a shelf behind them.

scenes.narration: Newspapers wrote about his debts, and many people wondered whether the Trump story was over.
scenes.caption: IS IT OVER?
scenes.picture: A commuter on a gray rainy Manhattan street reading a folded newspaper with a worried face, umbrellas and yellow taxis behind him.

scenes.narration: But one thing was still his: the name. So he began to rent it out.
scenes.caption: THE NAME
scenes.picture: Close-up of a hand holding a gleaming golden key above an open palm, a skyscraper blurred behind in warm light.

scenes.narration: Over the next decades, and especially in the 2000s, developers around the world paid to put his name on towers and hotels they built, though he still owned some properties.
scenes.caption: LICENSING
scenes.picture: A shining modern hotel tower rising over a distant coastal city skyline at sunrise, a gold sign glowing on its front, palm trees below.

scenes.narration: Now the name was everywhere. And he was still looking for a bigger stage.
scenes.caption: A BIGGER STAGE
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark suit stands alone on an empty theater stage in a single bright spotlight, rows of empty red seats before him.

scenes.narration: It arrived in January 2004, when NBC launched a reality show called The Apprentice.
scenes.caption: THE APPRENTICE, 2004
scenes.picture: A glossy television studio with bright lights and cameras, a polished dark conference table with a golden-lit skyline backdrop behind it.

scenes.narration: Each week, contestants competed in his boardroom, and each episode ended with two famous words: You're fired.
scenes.caption: YOU'RE FIRED
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark suit points his finger firmly across a boardroom table at a nervous young contestant, other contestants watching, dramatic lighting.

scenes.narration: Millions tuned in. Suddenly he wasn't only a New York builder. He was a household name in every state.
scenes.caption: EVERY STATE
scenes.picture: A farmhouse, a city apartment and a suburban home each with a television glowing blue through the window at night, joined by a starry sky.

scenes.narration: And it gave him something every politician wants: a face and a voice millions of Americans already knew.
scenes.caption: YEARS ON TV
scenes.picture: A grandmother and grandson sitting together on a small-town couch watching a television, popcorn bowl between them, cozy warm lamp.

scenes.narration: He had flirted with politics before: a brief Reform Party bid in 2000, and in 2011 he weighed a run, then said no.
scenes.caption: NOT YET
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a suit stands at a podium in an empty ballroom, hesitating, hand on the microphone, a sea of empty chairs in front of him.

scenes.narration: Then, on June 16, 2015, he rode down an escalator in Trump Tower and announced he was running for president.
scenes.caption: THE ESCALATOR
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark suit and red tie rides a long escalator downward in a glittering marble atrium with gold trim, a crowd waiting below.

scenes.narration: Experts gave him little chance. He was running against more than a dozen other Republicans, many of them governors and senators.
scenes.caption: LONG ODDS
scenes.picture: A long line of serious politicians in dark suits at a debate stage, Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a red tie standing at the far end in the spotlight.

scenes.narration: But he spoke plainly, filled arenas, and dominated the news. One by one, his rivals dropped out.
scenes.caption: MOMENTUM
scenes.picture: A huge indoor arena packed with a cheering crowd, Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), at a podium with arms raised, red, white and blue streamers falling from the ceiling.

scenes.narration: In July 2016, Republicans made him their nominee. In November, he would face Hillary Clinton, a former secretary of state.
scenes.caption: THE NOMINEE
scenes.picture: A bright convention hall with balloons drifting down, Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark suit on the stage waving to a cheering crowd, spotlights sweeping.

scenes.narration: Most polls showed her ahead. But on election night, he won key states like Pennsylvania, Michigan and Wisconsin.
scenes.caption: ELECTION NIGHT
scenes.picture: A newsroom at night, anchors and staff gaping in disbelief at a giant glowing screen, coffee cups scattered on the desks.

scenes.narration: He won 304 electoral votes to Clinton's 227, even though she won about 2.9 million more votes nationwide.
scenes.caption: 304 TO 227
scenes.picture: A tall pile of paper ballots in a counting room beside a wooden ballot box, election workers in the background, bright overhead light.

scenes.narration: On January 20, 2017, the former reality-show host became the forty-fifth president of the United States.
scenes.caption: 45TH PRESIDENT
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark overcoat raises his right hand on the steps of the white-domed Capitol, an enormous crowd stretching below in cold sunshine.

scenes.narration: In his first year, he signed a major tax cut, and his pick, Neil Gorsuch, joined the Supreme Court.
scenes.caption: FIRST TERM
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), at a large wooden desk in the Oval Office signs a document with a thick pen, aides in dark suits standing behind him.

scenes.narration: He named three justices in all, and in 2018 he met North Korea's leader, Kim Jong Un, in Singapore.
scenes.caption: THREE JUSTICES
scenes.picture: Two men in dark suits shake hands in front of a row of flags with no emblems in an elegant hotel hall, photographers crowding in.

scenes.narration: But in December 2019, the House impeached him over his dealings with Ukraine. In February 2020, the Senate acquitted him.
scenes.caption: FIRST IMPEACHMENT
scenes.picture: The grand wooden chamber of the Senate, rows of senators in dark suits seated at old wooden desks under bright chandeliers, a solemn mood.

scenes.narration: Weeks later, COVID-19 forced widespread shutdowns, so by May his administration launched Operation Warp Speed to speed up vaccines.
scenes.caption: COVID-19, 2020
scenes.picture: A lone scientist in a white lab coat and face mask examines a glowing vial in a bright laboratory, rows of vials racked behind.

scenes.narration: Then came November 2020. Joe Biden won the election, 306 electoral votes to 232.
scenes.caption: 2020 ELECTION
scenes.picture: Election workers in face masks carry sealed ballot boxes across a big bright counting hall, a long line of voters waiting outside.

scenes.narration: Trump said the vote was stolen. But courts rejected dozens of lawsuits, and election officials found no fraud that changed the result.
scenes.caption: THE DISPUTE
scenes.picture: A stern judge in a black robe at a tall wooden bench looks down at a stack of case files in a hushed courtroom, lawyers standing before him.

scenes.narration: On January 6, 2021, he spoke at a rally near the White House, and then a crowd marched to the Capitol.
scenes.caption: JANUARY 6, 2021
scenes.picture: A crowd in winter coats walks along a broad avenue toward the white-domed Capitol under a gray sky, cold breath in the air.

scenes.narration: Rioters broke in while Congress was counting the electoral votes. Lawmakers fled, and the count paused for hours.
scenes.caption: THE CAPITOL RIOT
scenes.picture: Broken glass and smashed doors at a grand marble hallway of the Capitol, scattered papers on the floor, dim emergency lighting, no people in focus.

scenes.narration: Congress finished in the early hours of January 7 and confirmed Biden. A week later, the House impeached Trump a second time, for incitement of insurrection.
scenes.caption: SECOND IMPEACHMENT
scenes.picture: The lit-up Capitol dome at night, a few lights glowing in windows, soldiers in winter coats standing guard outside under floodlights.

scenes.narration: In February, the Senate voted 57 to 43 to convict, short of the two-thirds needed, so he was acquitted again.
scenes.caption: LEAVING
scenes.picture: A tense Senate chamber, a senator standing at a desk to cast a vote, others seated in rows with solemn faces, soft light from tall windows.

scenes.narration: By then he had already left Washington, and many commentators wrote that his political career was over.
scenes.caption: ACQUITTED AGAIN
scenes.picture: A white and green presidential helicopter lifts off from a bare green lawn in front of the White House on a clear morning, no snow, bare trees around it.

scenes.narration: And in November 2022, he announced he was running again, from his Florida home, Mar-a-Lago.
scenes.caption: RUNNING AGAIN
scenes.picture: A grand pink-walled Florida mansion with a tall tower, palm trees and a glittering ballroom with a stage, warm evening light.

scenes.narration: Then the courts came. In 2023 he was indicted four times, in New York, Florida, Washington and Georgia, and pleaded not guilty.
scenes.caption: FOUR INDICTMENTS
scenes.picture: A tall stone courthouse with wide steps and columns on a gray morning, a dark motorcade parked at the curb, reporters waiting at a distance.

scenes.narration: On May 30, 2024, a Manhattan jury convicted him on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records.
scenes.caption: THE VERDICT
scenes.picture: A wood-paneled New York courtroom, a jury of twelve ordinary people seated in two rows, a judge's bench above, Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark suit seated at the defense table.

scenes.narration: It was the first time a former American president had been convicted of a crime. He denied wrongdoing and vowed to appeal.
scenes.caption: A FIRST
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark suit and red tie walks down a courthouse hallway with a stony expression, aides trailing behind him.

scenes.narration: Then, on July 13, at a rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, a gunman fired, and a bullet struck the upper part of Trump's right ear.
scenes.caption: BUTLER, PENNSYLVANIA
scenes.picture: An outdoor summer rally stage under a blue sky, Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark suit ducking behind a podium as agents in sunglasses rush toward him.

scenes.narration: One spectator was killed and two were wounded. Trump rose, blood on his face, and raised his fist.
scenes.caption: FIST IN THE AIR
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), a small red mark on his ear, stands raised up among dark-suited agents, fist in the air, a clear blue sky behind him, determined face.

scenes.narration: A week later, President Biden ended his reelection bid, and Vice President Kamala Harris became the Democratic nominee.
scenes.caption: A NEW RIVAL
scenes.picture: An empty presidential podium in front of a plain blue curtain, a single microphone, soft lights and a sense of silence.

scenes.narration: On November 5, 2024, Trump won, 312 electoral votes to 226. He carried all seven swing states and the popular vote.
scenes.caption: NOVEMBER 5, 2024
scenes.picture: A cheering crowd in a big hall with red, white and blue balloons and confetti, Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark suit on stage with arms wide.

scenes.narration: On January 20, 2025, he took the oath again, the second president, after Grover Cleveland, to serve two non-consecutive terms.
scenes.caption: SECOND OATH
scenes.picture: Donald Trump, drawn as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, pursed lips, dark suit and long red tie), in a dark overcoat takes the oath with his hand raised, a thick closed Bible held before him, under the golden high dome of the Capitol rotunda.

scenes.narration: From his father's building sites in Queens to the Capitol Rotunda, the name on the front of the tower carried him to Washington twice.
scenes.caption: THE NAME
scenes.picture: A lone tall skyscraper on the Manhattan skyline at dusk, its windows glowing gold, the quiet Queens rooftops in the foreground below, soft purple sky.

narrator: Epic historical narrator, deep and confident, dramatic swells, quick through action, slower only for the final line.

short.title: How Trump Came Back Twice
short.description:
How did a builder's son from Queens, New York, win back the White House in 2025? The short story of Donald Trump's rise, fall and return.
Sources: Library of Congress; National Archives; Associated Press election results.

scenes.narration: Donald Trump was written off twice, and twice he came back bigger.
scenes.picture: Close-up of Donald Trump as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, dark suit, long red tie), half his face in shadow and half in golden light, the White House glowing behind him at night

scenes.narration: He grew up in Queens, watching his father Fred build apartment blocks.
scenes.picture: a stern father in a 1950s suit and hat holding blueprints beside a small blond boy, young Donald Trump, red brick apartment blocks with scaffolding behind

scenes.narration: But Donald wanted Manhattan.
scenes.picture: young Donald Trump, a cartoon caricature with thick swept blond hair, on a Queens riverbank at dusk gazing across the water at the glittering Manhattan skyline

scenes.narration: So in 1983 he opened Trump Tower, with his name on the front.
scenes.picture: Donald Trump as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, dark suit, long red tie) standing proudly with arms spread in front of a tall black-glass skyscraper on Fifth Avenue

scenes.narration: Then he borrowed big, and by 1991 his Atlantic City casino was bankrupt.
scenes.picture: Donald Trump as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, dark suit, long red tie) sitting alone on an empty casino floor among dark, switched-off slot machines, worried face

scenes.narration: Papers said he was finished. So he rented out what he still had: his name.
scenes.picture: Donald Trump as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, dark suit, long red tie) holding up a gleaming golden key and smiling slyly, skyscrapers behind him

scenes.narration: Then The Apprentice put that name on TV in every state.
scenes.picture: Donald Trump as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, dark suit, long red tie) at a dark boardroom table pointing his finger at a nervous young contestant, bright studio lights

scenes.narration: In 2016, already famous, he beat Hillary Clinton for the presidency.
scenes.picture: Donald Trump as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, dark suit, long red tie) in a dark overcoat raising his right hand on the steps of the white-domed Capitol, huge crowd below

scenes.narration: But in 2020 he lost, was impeached again, and many called him finished.
scenes.picture: Donald Trump as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, dark suit, long red tie) walking away alone across a gray, empty White House lawn toward a waiting helicopter, cloudy sky

scenes.narration: Then came a criminal conviction, and a bullet that struck his ear.
scenes.picture: Donald Trump as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, dark suit, long red tie) raising his fist on an outdoor rally stage, a small red mark on his ear, agents in dark suits around him, blue sky

scenes.narration: Yet in 2024 he won again, carrying all seven swing states.
scenes.picture: Donald Trump as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, dark suit, long red tie) smiling with arms wide on a stage, red, white and blue balloons and confetti falling

scenes.narration: Written off twice, back twice: the builder's son returned to the White House.
scenes.picture: Donald Trump as a clearly recognisable cartoon caricature (swept blond hair, broad face, dark suit, long red tie) under the golden dome of the Capitol Rotunda, hand raised taking the oath, solemn and determined
